text:
maria (Support): FYI customer acme-inc reporting a cluster of 429s starting ~09:12 UTC. They have a Dedicated reserved commit but spikes look like short bursts coming from a single NATed egress IP. They say different teams use different API keys. Can we triage?

support-bot: New ticket created: #SR-89321 - rate-limit surge (auto-tag: nat-ip, multi-key)

dan (SRE): Can you paste a raw curl and one of the response headers from customer? need x-rate-limit headers to see which quota is triggering.

maria (Support): Pasted from customer: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-type: org
x-rate-limit-limit: 3600/hour
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c
```
They claim project-level quotas show plenty of headroom.

kevin (Runtime Eng): Interesting that header says type=org. Do they have an org-level burst cap? reserved commit shouldn't be affected by org quota for dedicated tenants, unless routing matched a fallback path. Any chance requests routed to hosted pool?

maria (Support): Customer insists traffic hits their Dedicated pool. They gave logs showing request host header set to dedicated.redwood.example.com and API key X-ACME-PROD.

dan (SRE): Two quick repros to ask customer: 1) curl with API key A (their project key) 2) curl using same egress NAT IP but a different API key from another project. We want to see whether quota is keyed by API key or by source IP. Example test: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-AAA" https://dedicated.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

alice (Billing): If org headers are hitting 0 remaining, billing/commit view will still show usage — but the org-level cap could be an override limit applied on edge for fraud protection or abuse. Check account console for any manual org caps.

sre-oncall (PagerDuty): I pulled edge routing logs for their IP 34.122.45.8 between 09:10-09:20 UTC. Looks like 70% of requests were routed to dedicated, 30% got routed to hosted fallback during an autoscale event. The hosted fallback would apply org-level rate limiting.

kevin (Runtime Eng): That matches a known corner case: when Dedicated capacity transiently underprovisions during scale events, smart routing can fallback to hosted variants which enforce org-scoped throttles. Two actionable items: 1) check dedicated autoscale logs for spike at 09:11-09:13 2) ask customer to rotate/centralize API keys so we can attribute per-key counters.

maria (Support): Customer provided quick repro showing both keys hit 429 at same second. They also provided a pcap confirming one outbound NAT IP. They asked: why do two different API keys see the same org 429?

dan (SRE): Because hosted fallback enforces org-level throttle across keys and IPs. If requests for both keys were routed to the hosted pool, the hosted org quota counters apply. That explains identical x-rate-limit headers.

kevin (Runtime Eng): Long-term fix: we should surface an explicit header when fallback occurs, e.g., x-fallback-target: hosted, and add an event to audit logs. Short term: increase transient capacity for that Dedicated fleet or whitelist this org's hosted quota during the burst window.

alice (Billing): I'll check whether they have a manual org cap or safety hold. If there is one I can lift it for a 30m window. Maria, can you get permission from customer for a temporary bump?

maria (Support): Asked customer for permission; they're OK with +30m bump. Also asked them to run the two-curl repro and paste responses.

sre-oncall (PagerDuty): I pushed a short autoscale tweak to reduce fallback for that pool (config change id: autoscale-2026-03-17-a1). Will monitor for next 15m.

maria (Support): Customer ran repro after bump: first call succeeded, second call still saw 429 but with header x-fallback-target: hosted. They attached this snippet: 
```
> GET /v1/generate
< HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
< x-rate-limit-type: org
< x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
< x-fallback-target: hosted
```
They also sent a small request sample that shows 150 rps burst for ~10s from the single NAT IP.

kevin (Runtime Eng): That confirms fallback path. I'll open a runtime ticket to (A) set a visible header for fallback, (B) add an audit event, (C) evaluate if we can prefer queued-burst handling with per-key isolation rather than org-level enforcement when traffic originates from Dedicated tenants.

dan (SRE): For immediate support we recommended customer: - rotate keys so critical clients use a dedicated long-lived key - if possible, split burst across multiple egress IPs - we (redwood) will temporarily raise hosted org throttle for them while autoscale settles.

maria (Support): Customer accepted. I created internal EPIC RED-4589 and linked SR-89321. I'll follow up once runtime ticket lands. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin (Runtime Eng): Note for postmortem: this is an auth-routing edge case where quota scope and routing target diverge. Adding to eng-runtime backlog.

maria (Support): Closing this Slack thread; moving conversation into SR-89321 thread for further notes. If anyone wants write access to the SR, ping me.
